extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and philosophers concerned with the foundations of calculus and geometry; readers of Berkeley's The Analyst
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical and mathematical critique that poses a series of questions evaluating the conceptual foundations of fluxions (early calculus), infinitesimals, geometry, and the methods of modern analysts. The page enumerates numbered queries probing clarity, meaning, and legitimacy of principles used in analytical mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Object of Geometry be not the Proportions of affignable Extenſions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether geometry's proper object is relations among assignable (finite) magnitudes, challenging appeal to infinite or infinitesimal magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the end of Geometry be not to meaſure aſſignable finite Extenſion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether practical measurement of finite magnitudes should be the true goal of geometry rather than metaphysical notions of the infinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistaking object and end
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the miſtaking the Object and End of Geometry hath not created needleſs Difficulties, and wrong Purſuits in that Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probes whether conceptual errors about what geometry studies have led to needless paradoxes and incorrect methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific method requires clear conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Men may properly be ſaid to proceed in a ſcientific Method, without clearly conceiving the Object they are converſant about, the End propoſed, and the Method by which it is purſued?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insists that scientific procedure presupposes clear notions of object, goal, and method; lack thereof undermines claims to science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignability suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it doth not ſuffice, that for every affignable number of Parts may be ſubjoin W contained in ſome aſſignable Magnitude ? And whether it be not unneceſſary, as well as abſurd, to ſuppose that finite Extenſion is infinitely diviſible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the need to posit actual infinite divisibility beyond any assignable partition; advocates consideration of assignable subdivisions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagrams as signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Diagrams in a Geometrical Demonſtration are not to be conſidered, as Signs of all poſſible finite Figures, of all ſenſible and imaginable Extenſions or Magnitudes of the ſame kind?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that diagrams should be viewed as general signs representing all particular finite cases, not as objects possessing actual infinite structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeing geometry from abstract extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be poſſible to free Geometry from inſuperable Difficulties and Abſurdities, ſo long as either the abſtract general Idea of Extenſion, or abſolute extenſion, be ſuppoſed its true Object ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether abandoning abstract/absolute notions of extension is necessary to avoid paradoxes in geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notions of absolute time/place/motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Notions of abſolute Time, - abſolute Place, and abſolute Motion be not moſt abſtractedly Metaphyſical? Whether it be poſsible for us to meaſure, compute, or know them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions the meaningfulness and utility of absolute metaphysical concepts in mathematical and empirical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: On conceiving velocities independent of measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether we can form an Idea or Notion of Extenſion prior to Motion? Or whether if a Man had never perveived Motion, he would ever have known or conceived one thing to be diſtant from another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores the dependence of geometric notions (extension, distance) on perception of motion; questions purely abstract conceptions disconnected from perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximating curves by polygons
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether in ey it m not ſuffice to conſider affignable finite Mg nitude, without concerning our ſelves with Infinity? And whether it would not be righter to meaſure large Polygons having ſuppoſe Curves are Polygons of infidiceſſmal Sides, a Suppolition l he true nor conceivable ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the common assumption that curves are literally polygons with infinitesimal sides; promotes using finite approximations without invoking actual infinitesimals.

rubrics_metrics.name: True-but-unreadily-accepted points
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether many Points, which are not readily aſſented to, are not nevertheleſs true?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admits that some unintuitive propositions may nevertheless be correct; prompts careful examination of disputed foundational claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension prior to motion (repeat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be poflible, that we ſhould have had an Idea or Notion of Extenſion prior to Motion? Or whether if a Man had never perveived Motion, he would ever have known or conceived one thing to be diſtant from another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeats interrogation of dependency of spatial ideas on motion/perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometrical quantity and consistent parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Oeometrical Quantity bath cocniſtent Parcs ? And whether all Quantity be not in a flux as well as Time and Motion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether geometrical quantities have consistent, stable parts or are in flux similarly to time and motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension as attribute of immutable being
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Extenſion can be ſupposed an Attribute of a Being Immutable and eternal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks metaphysical question about attributing extension to an immutable deity; probes coherence of such attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining principles vs. bigotry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to decline examining the Principles, and unravelling the Methods uſed in Mathematics, would not ſhew a bigotry in Mathematicians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for scrutiny of foundational principles rather than accepting methods unexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maxims among analysts vs good sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether certain Maxims do have current among, Analyſts, which are ing to good Senſe ? And whether the common Aſſumption that a finite Quantity divided by nothing is infinite be not of this Number?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques customary analytical maxims (e.g., dividing by zero) as contrary to common sense and potentially erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagrams considered absolutely cause error
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the conſidering Geometrical Diagrams abſalutely of in themſelves, rather than as Repreſentatives of all aſſignable Magnitudes or Figures of the ſame kind, be not a principal Cauſe of the ſuppoſing finire Extenſion infinite- ly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that treating diagrams as absolute entities (instead of representatives) leads to false inferences about infinite divisibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinite divisibility as hidden assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether om F do not ſuppoſe and imply, either general ſon to be the Object of Geometry? And, therefore, whether, along with thoſe Sup- Sub. WM bofitions, ſuch Arguments alſo do not It fol ceaſe and yaniſh ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges whether assuming infinite divisibility implicitly changes the object of geometry and undermines arguments (text fragmented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'contains more than any assignable parts'
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is ſaid or implied that ſuch a certain Line delineated on Paper contains more that any aſſignable number of Parts, whether any more in truth ought to be underſtood, than that it is a Sign indifferently representing all finite Lines, be they ever ſo great.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that saying a diagram 'contains more than any assignable number of parts' should mean it stands for all finite lines, not that the particular line literally has infinite parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snares of infinite divisibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the ſuppoſed infinite Diviſibility of finite Extenſion hath not been a Snare to Mathematicians, and aplied MW Thorn in their Sides? And whether a quantity infinitely diminiſhed and a Quantity infinitely ſmall are not the ſame thing in ching?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that assuming infinite divisibility misleads mathematicians; questions identity of 'infinitely diminished' and 'infinitely small' concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of velocities of nascent quantities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be neceſſary to In conſider Velocities of naſcent or eva- neſcent Quantities, or -Moments, or Infinitesimals? And whether the introducing alto* of Things ſo inconceivable be not a reproach to Mathematics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether mathematical practice legitimately needs to posit nascent velocities or infinitesimals that are conceptually obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admitting inconsistencies as truths
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Inconſiſtencies can be Truths? Whether Points repugnant and abſurd are to be admitted upon any Subject, or in any Science? And whether the uſe of Infinites ought to be allowed, as a ...?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the allowance of contradictory or absurd points within scientific reasoning and questions legitimacy of infinitesimals if they introduce contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known by proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a Quantity be not properly ſaid to be known, when we know its Proportion to given Quantities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes that knowledge of a quantity consists in knowing its ratio to other given quantities; emphasizes relational character of mathematical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression/notation as mathematical essence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Expreſſions or Notations of Quantity be defines their Uſe? in general Caſe of pure Algebra, we are at ſufficient Pretext and Apology, for the ad-
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises question about the role and limits of symbols and expressions: whether notation defines use and suffices as representation (fragmented in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of arithmetic operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the finding out propre not the moſt general Character and Tend- ency of the Mathematics? And Arithmetical Operation that which limits and ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks about the general aims of mathematics and the role of arithmetical operations in defining and limiting mathematical practice (text fragmented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Mathemaricians hat ſufficiently conſidered the and Uk of Signs? And how far the ſpecific limited Nature of things correſponds thereto?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Queries whether mathematicians have adequately reflected on symbolic notation and its correspondence (or lack thereof) to the specific nature of things represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: License of notation vs. geometric limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether becauſe, in ating ful liberty to make a Character denote, or nothing at all, we may therefore in a geometrical Caſe, limited by Hypotheſes and Reaſonings from particular Properties, claim the same Licence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against transferring the unconstrained symbolic liberties of algebra to geometrical reasoning where hypotheses limit acceptable moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shifting hypothesis is sophism
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Shifting of the Hypotheſis, or (as we may call it) the fallacia Sufppofitionis be not a Sophiſm, that far and wide infects the modern Reaſonings, both in the mechanical Philo- ſophy and in the abſtruſe and fine Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies an error — covertly changing hypotheses during reasoning — as a pervasive sophism in modern mathematical and natural philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity as distinct idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether we can form an Idea of Velocity diſtinct from and excluſive of its Meaſures, as we can of Heat diſtin& from and exclufive of the Degrees on the Thermometer, by which it is meaſured ? And whether this be not limit ſuppoſed in the Reaſonings of modern Analysts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether velocity can be conceived independently of its measures, and critiques analysts who treat velocities as abstracted from their measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/velocity conceivability in a point
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Motion can be conceived in Point of Space? And if Motion cannot, whether Velocity can? And if not, whether a firſt or laſt Velocity can be conceived in a mere Limit, either initial or final, of the deſcribed ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether motion or velocity make sense at a geometrical point or merely as limits; challenges notions of initial/final velocities in limit form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportions where no increments exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are no Increments, whether there can be any Ratio of Increments? Whether Nothings can be conſidered as proportional to real Quantities? Or whether to talk of their Proportions be not to talk Nonſenſe? Alſo in what Senſe we are to underſtand - the Proportion of a Surface to a Line, of an Area to an Ordinate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions legitimacy of talking about ratios involving zero/inexistent increments and cross-dimensional proportions (area to line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Squaring circles and equivalence of curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether if all aſſignable Circles may be ſquared, the Circle is not to all intents and purpoſes, ſquared as well as the Parabola? Or whether a parabolical Area can in fact be meaſured more accurately than a Circular?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probes the logic of 'squaring' curves and whether methods that square some assignable instances imply squaring other curves in principle or practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer approximation over sophistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be righter to approximate fairly, than to endeavour at Accuracy by Sophisms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates honest finite approximation rather than pursuing spurious exactness via dubious infinitesimal reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trials and inductions vs false demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it would not be more decent to proceed by Trials and Inductions, than to pretend to demonſtrate by falſe Principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests empirical/inductive methods may be preferable to demonstrations resting on unsound principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth without scientific principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there be not a way of arriving at Truth, although the Principles are not ſcientifie, nor the Reaſoning juſt? And whether ſuch a way ought to be called a Knack or a Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether practical methods yielding true results despite unsound principles deserve the name 'science' or merely 'knack'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of conclusion vs principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there can be Science of the Concluſion, where there is not Science of the Principles? And whether a Man can have Science of the Principles, without underſtanding them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether valid conclusions can constitute science if underlying principles are not understood; criticizes technicians who apply rules without grasping foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius foiled by false principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the greateſt Genius wreſtling with falſe Principles may not be foiled? And whether accurate Quadratures can be obtained without new Poſtulata or ? And if not, whether thoſe which are intelligible and conſiſtent ought not to be preferred to the contrary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that even great intellects can be misled by false principles; recommends preferring intelligible, consistent postulates if new axioms are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tedious calculation's effect on mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether tedious Calculations in Algebra and Fluxions be the liklieſt Method to improve the Mind ? And whether Mens being accuſtomed to reaſon altogether about Mathematical Signs and Figures, doth not make them at a loſs how to reaſon without them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether laborious symbolic calculations cultivate genuine understanding or merely facility with symbols, impairing reasoning without notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of analytical readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, whatever readineſs Analyſts acquire in ſtating a Problem, or finding apt Expreſſions for Mathematical Quantities, the ſame doth neceſſarily in- ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether skill in analytical expression translates to general intellectual abilities (text truncated); skeptical about automatic transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dividing equal products by same coefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be. not a general Caſe or Rule, that one and the ſame Coefficient dividing equal Products gives equal Quotients ? And yet whether ſuch Coefficient can be interpreted by 0 or nothing ? Or whether any one will fay, that if the Equation 2 xo = 5 No, be di- vided by 0, the Quotients on both Sides are equal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights pitfalls in algebraic manipulations, especially division by zero, warning that formal algebraic rules may fail or be illegitimate in singular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebra as science like geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether in the moſt general Reaſonings about Equalities and Propor- tions, Men may not demonſtrate as well as in Geometry? Whether in ſuch Demonſtrations, they are not obliged to the ſame ſtrict Reaſoning as in Geometry? Whether Algebra be not as truly a Science as Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether algebraic reasoning can be as rigorous and scientific as geometric demonstration, requiring similar standards of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning in species as in words
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Men may not reaſon in Species as well as in Words? Whether the Rules of Logic do not obtain in both Cases ? And whether we have not right to expect and demand the ſame Evidence in both ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues symbols ('species') should be held to the same logical standards as verbal reasoning; demands equal evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indulgence for obscure principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an Algebraiſt, Fluxio- niſt, Geometrician or Demonſtrator of any kind can expect indulgence for obſcure Principles or incorrect Reaſonings? And whether an Algebraical Note or Species in the end of a Process can be interpreted in a Sense which could not have been Subſtituted for it at the beginning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects leniency for obscure premises or post-hoc reinterpretation of symbols; insists consistency in interpretation from start to finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer vs man of science
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Difference be I” t between a mere Computer and a Man of Science be not, that the one computes on Principles clearly conceived, and by Rules evidently demonſtrated, whereas the other doth not?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws distinction between mere calculators and true scientists: the latter reason from clearly understood principles and justified rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical excellence vs false principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, though Geometry be a Science, and Algebra allowed to be a Science, and the Analytical a most excellent Method, in the Application nevertheless of the Analysis to Geometry, Men may not have admitted falſe Principles and wrong Methods of Reaſoning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges the value of analytic methods but warns that their application can still rely on false principles or faulty reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error when limiting signs to particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether although Algebraical Reaſonings are admitted to be ever fo juſt, when confined to Signs or Species as general Repreſentatives of Quantity, you may not nevertheleſs fall into Error, if, when you limit them to; ſtand for particular things, you do not limit yourself to reason consistently with the Nature of ſuch particular things?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautions that symbolic reasoning valid in the general may become erroneous when applied to particular cases unless the peculiar nature of the particulars is respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression by artifice vs science by deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the View of modern Mathematicians doth not rather ſeem to be the coming at an Expreſſion by Artifice, than the coming at Science by Deduction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizes focus on obtaining convenient expressions by algebraic artifice rather than deriving truly scientific understanding via sound deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of sound metaphysics/logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there may not be ſound Metaphyſics as well as unſound? Sound as well as unsound Logic? And whether the modern Analytics may not be brought under one of theſe Denominations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows that metaphysics and logic can be sound or unsound; invites classification of modern analytical methods accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental 'first philosophy'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there be not really Phileſophia prima, a certain tranſcendental Science ſuperior to and more intenſim than Mathematics, which it might be thought our modern Range recur en ken than deſpiſe ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests there may exist a higher foundational discipline (first philosophy) that undergirds mathematics and should not be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes among mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ever fince the recovery of Mathematical Learning, there have not been perpetual Diſputes and Controverſies among the Mathematicians ? And whether this doth not diſparage the Evidence of their Methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes continual controversies in mathematics and questions whether this undermines trust in methods and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphysics/logic to enlighten mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any thing but Metaphyſics and Logic can open the Eyes of Mathematicians and extricate them out of their Difficulties?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether philosophical analysis (metaphysics, logic) is necessary to resolve mathematical foundational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry's practical end implies approximations suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether if the end of Geometry be Practice, and this Practice be measuring aſſignable Extenſions, it will not follow that un- limited Approximations compleatly an- swer the Intention of Geometry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that if geometry's aim is practical measurement of assignable magnitudes, then unlimited finite approximations achieve the goal without invoking actual infinitesimals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do finite methods suffice for infinitesimal results
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the ſame things which are now done by Infinites may not be done by finite Quantities? And whether this would not be a great Relief to the Imaginations and Understandings of Mathematical Men?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests replacing infinitesimal methods with finite procedures that achieve the same results and are conceptually clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit faith in doctrine among practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether thoſe Philomathematical Phyſicians, Anatomſts, and Dealers in the Animal Oeconomy, who admit the modern Doctrine of Fluxions with an implicit Faith, can with a good grace inſult other Men for believing what they do not comprehend?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizes practitioners who accept fluxions by faith and demean others who resist unintelligible doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-emphasis on mathematical philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Corpuſcularian, Experimental, and Mathematical Philoſophy ſo much cultivated in the laſt Age, bath not too much engroſſed Mens Attention; ſome part whereof it might have uſefully employed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions whether the predominance of certain mathematical-natural philosophies has distracted intellectual resources from other useful pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative minds diminished
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether from this, and other concurring Cauſes, the Minds of ſpeculative Men have not been born downwards, ſtript of higher powers? ... whether we may not hence account for that prevailing Narrowneſs and Bigotry among many who paſs for Men of Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that methodological narrowness and overreliance on certain methods have reduced breadth of thought and promoted bigotry among some scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admiration for fluxions vs religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be really an Effect of Thinking, that the fame Men admire the great Author for his Fluxions, and deſpiſe other Men for their Religion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques intellectual arrogance: admiration for mathematical innovators coupled with contempt for religious convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith from effects vs demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be not a juſter way rather to derive Faith from their Effects, than to demonſtrate Mathematical Principles by theſe (text truncated)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether practical success (effects) should ground belief in principles rather than purported demonstrations founded on obscure reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admitting points above reason vs contrary to reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be not leſs exceptionable to admit Points above Reaſon than contrary to Reaſon ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between mysteries that may lie beyond current reason and propositions that positively contradict reason; the latter are more objectionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mysteries in divine vs human science
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Myſteries may not with better right be allowed of in Divine Faith, than in Humane Science ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues mysteries may be tolerable in faith but not in human scientific inquiry, which requires clarity and reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics of mysteries examine their principles?
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ſuch Mathematicians as cry out againſt Myſteries, have ever examined their own Principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges those who denounce mysteries elsewhere to reflect whether their own mathematical principles are free of similar obscurities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematicians' scruples in religion vs their science
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Mathematicians, who are ſo delicate in religious Points, are ſtrictly ſcrupulous in their own Science? Whether they do not ſubmit to Authority, take things upon Truſt, believe Points inconceivable ? Whether they have not their Myſteries, and what is more, their Re- pugnancies and Contradictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points out possible hypocrisy: being exacting in theological matters but uncritical about one's own scientific dogmas involving incomprehensible assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puzzled men to judge warily
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it might not become Men, who are puzzled and perplexed about their own Principles, to judge wari- ly, candidly, and modeſtly concerning other Matters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges intellectual humility: those uncertain about their own foundations should be cautious in judging other domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytics as argument against infidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the modern Analytia do not furniſh a ſtrong argumentum ad hominem, againſt the Philomathematical infidels of theſe Times?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that modern analytical methods, by exposing obscurities, supply rhetorical ammunition against certain infidel positions (context rhetorical).
